title: A Van Gogh Painting Sells for a Record $190.4 Million
summary: A painting by Vincent van Gogh has sold for a record $190.4 million. The auction house Sotheby's sold Chestnut Trees in Blossom in New York on Wednesday, November 19. The sale broke Van Gogh's old auction record of $117.2 million, set in 2022. Before the sale, experts thought the painting was worth about $180 million. No one knows yet who bought it. Van Gogh painted it in 1890, in the last two months of his life. Sotheby's calls it one of the most important works of art from that time still owned by a private family. The sale happened only after a last-minute deal settled a fight about the painting's past. People speaking for the heirs of the Fischer family, who owned it long ago in Germany, said it may have been sold under pressure when the Nazis were rising to power. Sotheby's said the two families reached a deal both sides were happy with. The Blaquier family had owned the painting since 1975, for more than 50 years.
why_it_matters: Art from long ago can still matter today, and learning about who owned a painting helps us understand history.
